cases.title: Tube heat-transfer estimate B

cases.title: Pipe pressure-drop estimate
cases.context: A Newtonian fluid of density 1000 kg/m3 flows at 2.5 m/s through a diameter 0.02 m tube with viscosity 0.001 Pa s. The solver obtains Re = 50000 and uses the Hagen–Poiseuille pressure-drop law.

options.label: C

cases.title: Pipe friction-factor estimate
cases.context: A Newtonian fluid has density 1000 kg/m3, speed 1 m/s, pipe diameter 0.02 m and viscosity 0.001 Pa s. The solver obtains Re = 20000 and uses the Darcy friction factor f = 64/Re.

cases.title: Slab cooling estimate
cases.context: A slab has convection coefficient h = 100 W/(m2 K), characteristic length L = 0.01 m, and conductivity k = 2 W/(m K). The solver obtains Bi = 0.5 and uses a lumped-capacitance temperature history.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The given conductivity should be multiplied by the characteristic length to compute Bi.

options.label: B
options.text: The lumped-temperature assumption fails its Bi criterion.

options.label: C
options.text: Bi should be 0.05.

cases.title: Part cooling estimate
cases.context: A part has h = 20 W/(m2 K), characteristic length L = 0.01 m, and k = 1 W/(m K). The solver obtains Bi = 0.2 and models the internal temperature as uniform.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The characteristic length should be omitted from the Bi calculation.

options.label: B
options.text: Bi arithmetic is wrong.

options.label: C
options.text: The uniform-temperature assumption is outside its domain.

cases.title: Arrhenius rate estimate
cases.context: An empirical Arrhenius fit used measurements from 300 K to 350 K. At reference temperature 300 K, its fitted rate constant is 1 s^-1 and its fitted Ea/R is 1500 K. The solver evaluates k(T) = k(300 K) exp[-(Ea/R)(1/T - 1/300 K)] at 500 K and reports k = 7.389 s^-1.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The prediction extrapolates beyond the temperatures used to fit the Arrhenius parameters.

options.label: B
options.text: Arrhenius temperature must be expressed in Celsius.

options.label: C
options.text: The prediction interpolates between measured fit temperatures.

cases.title: Henry-law partial-pressure estimate
cases.context: An empirical Henry-law fit used liquid solute mole fractions from 0.001 to 0.05. Its fitted Henry coefficient is H = 100 kPa per unit mole fraction. The solver substitutes x = 0.2 into p = H x and reports p = 20 kPa.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the engineering issue?

options.label: A
options.text: The mole fraction must be converted to mol/L before using the stated fit.

options.label: B
options.text: The calculation extrapolates beyond the fit compositions.

options.label: C
options.text: The substitution is within the fit compositions.

cases.title: Carbon dioxide density estimate
cases.context: Carbon dioxide at T = 310 K and P = 7.0 MPa has critical temperature Tc = 304.13 K and critical pressure Pc = 7.3773 MPa. With molar mass M = 0.04401 kg/mol and R = 8.314 J/(mol K), the solver obtains reduced temperature Tr = 1.0193 and ideal-gas density rho = 119.53 kg/m3.

options.label: B
options.text: The reduced-temperature arithmetic is inconsistent with the inputs.

options.label: C
options.text: Ideal-gas density is appropriate at this state.

cases.context: A dense cell culture has a scattering coefficient of 20 cm^-1 across a 0.2 cm optical path. The solver obtains scattering optical depth 4. options.label: B
options.text: Multiple scattering makes the single-pass absorption calibration unreliable.

options.label: C
options.text: The scattering optical-depth multiplication is incorrect.

cases.title: Steady mixer flow account
cases.context: At steady state with no reaction or storage, mass enters a mixer at 5 kg/s and 5 kg/s. Its only reported outlet is 8 kg/s. Measurement tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: A 2 kg/s unreported outlet or leak could explain the deficit.

options.label: B
options.text: The streams balance exactly.

options.label: C
options.text: An unreported inlet could account for the measured outlet deficit.

cases.title: Separator flow account
cases.context: A steady nonreacting separator has inlet mass flow 10 kg/s and reported outlets 6 kg/s and 6 kg/s. There is no storage; tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: A missing outlet explains the excess.

options.label: B
options.text: The 2 kg/s outlet excess suggests an unreported inlet or meter error.

options.label: C
options.text: The mass balance closes.

cases.title: Dryer flow account
cases.context: A steady dryer has total inlet mass 4 kg/s and reported outlet streams of 3 kg/s and 2 kg/s, including evaporated material. No accumulation occurs; tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: Evaporation accounts for the extra total outlet mass.

options.label: B
options.text: The balance closes.

options.label: C
options.text: An outlet meter over-read or unreported inlet could explain the 1 kg/s excess.

cases.title: Pipe-junction flow account
cases.context: At a steady pipe junction, two inlet flows are 2 kg/s and 3 kg/s, and measured outlets are 1 kg/s and 2 kg/s. No storage or reaction occurs; tolerance is 0.01 kg/s.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 2 kg/s shortfall suggests a leak or omitted outlet.

options.label: B
options.text: The four streams satisfy continuity.

options.label: C
options.text: Pressure loss accounts for the difference between total inlet and outlet mass flow.

cases.title: Heater energy account
cases.context: A steady heater receives 100 kW in the process stream and 20 kW electric power. The only reported output is 110 kW in the process stream; heat loss is stated zero and tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The electrical power can be omitted from the energy balance because it is converted to heat.

options.label: B
options.text: The missing 10 kW indicates an unmeasured loss or a meter error.

options.label: C
options.text: Energy closes to tolerance.

cases.title: Turbine energy account
cases.context: A steady adiabatic turbine receives 500 kW of inlet energy flow and reports 400 kW outlet energy flow plus 120 kW shaft power. Changes in stored energy are zero; tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The extra shaft power can be attributed to an unreported heat loss.

options.label: B
options.text: The energy balance closes.

options.label: C
options.text: The 20 kW reported output excess suggests an over-read or omitted input.

cases.title: Heat-exchanger energy account
cases.context: Across the whole steady insulated exchanger, inlet enthalpy flows total 200 kW and 300 kW; outlet flows are 250 kW and 240 kW. No work or accumulation occurs; tolerance is 0.1 kW.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The 10 kW output deficit suggests heat leakage or a measurement error.

options.label: B
options.text: Heat transfer between the two sides can account for the whole-exchanger deficit.

options.label: C
options.text: The whole-exchanger balance closes.

cases.title: Battery discharge energy account
cases.context: Over a stated discharge interval, measured stored-energy decrease is 50 kJ and electrical input is 0 kJ. Electrical output is 40 kJ and measured heat output is 15 kJ. No other transfers or storage changes occur; tolerance is 0.1 kJ.
cases.question: Which choice identifies the contradiction and a plausible explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The electrical output alone accounts for the stored-energy decrease.

options.label: B
options.text: The 5 kJ output excess indicates a measurement or accounting error.

options.label: C
options.text: The energy account closes.
